# gh-1888 re-review: Findings 3, 4, 5 verification (report part 1/2 — Finding 3)

Environment note: this investigation sandbox has NO shell/exec tool, so `git diff 2c6a49ce38..HEAD` and `dart test` could NOT be run. All verdicts below are from reading the code at HEAD directly; test files were read in full and assert exactly the claimed behaviors.

## Finding 3 — private membership misclassified as PUBLIC → plaintext downgrade: VERIFIED

**(a) Stored-shape decision — implemented as claimed.**
- `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart:228-246` `_isPublicChannel`: decision comes from `scoped.union().then((u) => u.effective())` — the STORED union — with `membership.pub == null` as the public test (lines 237-242). Comment at 232-236 states the exact rationale (undecryptable envelope must not downgrade frames). Runtime decryption success no longer decides wire format.
- `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart:206-226` `privateChannelKeyMissing`: stored-private = any stored membership matching the channel with `pub != null` (215-217); key-missing = no runtime membership with `priv != null` (219-222). Note runtimeEffective() re-attaches `_memoryOnlyKeys` when `m.priv == null` (bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart runtimeEffective), so memory-only keys correctly count as resolved.
- `bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart:144-155`: for `#` targets, after the public branch (134-143), the guard throws `StateError('refusing to send to #…: the private channel key is unavailable …')` before `sendChannelFanet1` (158).
- Wiring confirmed: `bin/fah_model.dart` `_resolvePlugins` constructs `HubFabricRepository` with `publicChannelChecker: HubPluginHost.publicChannelFor` and `privateKeyMissingChecker: HubPluginHost.privateChannelKeyMissing` — both checkers are live in production, not test-only.

**(b) No send-path bypass.**
- `HubFabricRepository` has exactly one outbound method: `send` (127). peek/drain are inbound; register/touch are no-ops; directory is read-only. No internal retry/queue in the adapter.
- The only retry/queue path is `FallbackMessagingRepository._flushQueued` (lib/src/messaging/fallback_messaging_repository.dart), which forwards via `_primary.send(...)` — the same guarded send (per-message `try/on Object { break; }` keeps the queue on failure).
- DM path (`repo.send`, hub_fabric_repository.dart:161-168) never touches channels. The `dap_*` tools are DM-only: `dap_send`→`_executeDapDm` sends a hub DM via `_hub.repository` (bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart:~1843, recipient "16-hex agent id or display name", not `#channel`); channel writes per the boot notice go only through `agent_message to: "#channel"` → the fabric composite.

**(c) StateError is caught upstream — no agent-loop crash.**
- `FallbackMessagingRepository.send` lib/src/messaging/fallback_messaging_repository.dart:82-88: `try { await _primary.send(...) } on Object { ... }` — the refusal StateError is swallowed and the message lands in the file fabric (96) + `_trackForForward` (97): it queues and retries on reconnect, exactly the claimed "queues/retries" semantics.
- `_flushQueued` retry of the same message also catches per-message (break, keeps queued). Final backstop: `bin/fah.dart` main `runZoned` handler routes hub-teardown errors to a stderr line, not a crash.

**(d) Stored shape used for ALL scopes.** `union()` (bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart) merges global (`_loadLegacyKeys`, ~/.dap files), project (`.fah/dap.json`), session (JSONL records), and env (`DAP_CHANNELS_JSON`) — and both checkers read the stored union first, then `runtimeEffective()`. No path surfaces a stored-private membership with `priv == null` at runtime without the guard firing; if either checker itself errors, it returns false (`on Object → false`, fah_hub_plugin.dart:223-225, 243-245) which falls to the fanet1 (encrypted) branch — a client-side send failure caught by the composite, never a plaintext downgrade. Fail direction is safe in every error arm.

**(e) Test exists and asserts no wire frame.** test/hub/hub_fabric_repository_test.dart:150-181: asserts `StateError` whose message contains 'refusing to send to #locked' and 'key', then asserts nothing reached the wire via a 300 ms inbound timeout against a real FakeHub.

**Residual risks (minor):**
1. "Loudly" is only loud internally — the composite's `on Object` catch swallows the refusal reason with no log line; the sender-visible effect is silent queue-and-retry (boot-time `loadWarnings` do warn about the missing passphrase, so the user is told once at boot).
2. A malformed stored membership with `priv != null` but `pub == null` at rest classifies as PUBLIC (pub==null rule) → plaintext. Requires a corrupt record; theoretical only.
